# Results — Study 246 (Defensive-Sectors Leadership) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The combined XLP+XLU/SPY
relative-strength momentum signal (20-day change in the average sector RS, rolling 252-day
percentile rank) sorted into quintiles, tested against forward SPY log-returns at 1-day,
5-day, and 21-day horizons, and as a binary timing overlay (go to cash in the top 20% alert
quintile). Auto-adjusted daily closes from Yahoo Finance. As-of **2026-06-16**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | Fingerprint (SPY_close) |
|---|---|---|
| XLP, XLU, SPY | 1998-12-23 → 2026-06-16 | `e4ade1bcf806` |

n = **6,911** trading days (~27.5 years).

## The quintile test — does combined defensive leadership point the right way?

Sort each day by the rolling percentile rank of the 20-day combined (XLP+XLU)/SPY RS
momentum into five buckets (Q1 = SPY outperforming / calm; Q5 = defensives outperforming
strongly / alert) and measure forward SPY log-returns. The folk claim predicts a
**monotone descent** from Q1 to Q5.

### 1-day forward returns

| Quintile | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 (calm) | 1,315 | **+2.46** | +0.95 |
| Q2 | 1,330 | +0.09 | +0.04 |
| Q3 | 1,422 | **+5.42** | +1.93 |
| Q4 | 1,290 | +3.78 | +1.18 |
| Q5 (alert) | 1,471 | +4.02 | +1.09 |

The 1-day pattern is **non-monotone**: Q3 is the highest quintile, Q5 is higher than Q1.
No meaningful predictive tilt at the daily horizon.

### 5-day forward returns

| Quintile | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 (calm) | 1,315 | **+29.71** | **+3.04** |
| Q2 | 1,330 | +7.96 | +0.99 |
| Q3 | 1,421 | +10.92 | +1.22 |
| Q4 | 1,287 | +5.38 | +0.48 |
| Q5 (alert) | 1,471 | +24.79 | +1.79 |

At 5 days the pattern is also **non-monotone**: Q5 is the second-highest quintile,
nearly matching Q1. The folk narrative is violated by the data.

### 21-day forward returns (1-month horizon)

| Quintile | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 (calm) | 1,306 | **+112.10** | **+4.69** |
| Q2 | 1,328 | +68.24 | +2.75 |
| Q3 | 1,417 | +44.86 | +1.71 |
| Q4 | 1,286 | +44.40 | +1.26 |
| Q5 (alert) | 1,471 | **+68.48** | +2.27 |

At 21 days there is a broadly downward trend from Q1 to Q4, but Q5 reverses back above
Q3 and Q4. This non-monotone break means the full pattern contradicts the "orderly
risk-off descent" claim:

## The decisive test — Q1 (calm) vs Q5 (alert) spread

| Horizon | Q1 mean (bps) | Q5 mean (bps) | Spread (Q1−Q5) | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day | +2.46 | +4.02 | **−1.56** | **−0.42** |
| 5-day | +29.71 | +24.79 | **+4.93** | **+0.11** |
| 21-day | +112.10 | +68.48 | **+43.62** | **+0.79** |

**The decisive Q1−Q5 spread fails at every horizon.**  At 1-day the spread is actually
*negative* (Q5 earns more than Q1), and the 21-day spread of +43.6 bps achieves only
*t* = +0.79 — far below the inference bar of 2.0.  This is unambiguously weaker than
the single-sector utilities canary (Study 131: *t* = +1.58 at 21d), suggesting that
adding consumer staples (XLP) to the mix does not sharpen the signal.

## Regime statistics (50/50 split at the combined RS median)

| Regime | n | mean (bps/day) | Annualised Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Full sample | 6,909 | +3.31 | +0.433 | +2.60 |
| Calm (def Q1–Q2) | 3,483 | **+3.36** | **+0.521** | +2.12 |
| Alert (def Q3–Q5) | 3,426 | +3.27 | +0.376 | +1.52 |

The Sharpe split (0.52 vs 0.38) is present but much smaller than the single-sector
utilities case (0.70 vs 0.22). More importantly, the **mean return difference is
essentially zero** (+3.36 vs +3.27 bps/day) — the regime Sharpe difference is almost
entirely a volatility effect with negligible return component.

## Binary timing overlay — cash in the top 20% defensive alert days

| Cost (bps/switch) | Spread mean (bps/day) | HAC *t* | Active Sharpe |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (gross) | −0.77 | −1.04 | +0.430 |
| 0.5 | −0.80 | −1.09 | +0.424 |
| 1.0 | −0.84 | −1.13 | +0.418 |
| 2.0 | −0.91 | −1.23 | +0.406 |
| 5.0 | −1.11 | −1.51 | +0.371 |

The active strategy has a **lower Sharpe than buy-and-hold** even at zero cost (0.430 vs
0.432 passive). The gross alpha is −0.77 bps/day — there is no break-even cost. With
480 round-trip switches over 27.5 years, every basis point of execution cost accelerates
the deterioration.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.**  The decisive Q1−Q5 spread is *negative* at 1-day (wrong direction)
  and only +43.6 bps at 21-day (*t* = +0.79, far below the bar of 2). The quintile
  pattern is non-monotone at all horizons. Combining XLP and XLU does not improve on (and
  in fact slightly weakens) the single-sector utilities canary (Study 131). The folk
  claim finds no statistical support.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.**  The timing overlay produces a *lower Sharpe* than buy-and-hold
  even before costs (0.430 vs 0.432). Gross daily alpha = −0.77 bps (*t* = −1.04). No
  break-even cost exists; the strategy destroys value at every tested cost level.
- **Coincident or forecast?**  The combined defensive RS momentum tags episodes of market
  stress but — as with Study 131 — does not statistically precede weak SPY returns. The
  signal is at best coincident, more likely a *consequence* of the same volatility regime
  it claims to forecast.
